sentences.text: Suppression planning begins after the Caldera Incident Command Portal promotes an accepted fire location into the operational map and marks it available for aviation review.
The Air Attack Supervisor reviews the promoted location, the confidence history, and the current airspace status before authorizing reconnaissance or retardant planning.
The Drone Tasking Service converts reconnaissance objectives into trackable missions with launch windows, image requirements, altitude limits, and abort criteria.
Horizon Ridge Drone Dock supports initial attack by keeping assigned aircraft charged, positioned, and ready for rapid launch when mission approval is granted.
Kestrel is required to report launch readiness, aircraft health, and recovery availability before a reconnaissance task can be released.
The Drone Pilot Operator confirms that the proposed route is consistent with field conditions and can be flown without interfering with suppression aircraft.
Reconnaissance imagery is used to verify access, flame spread direction, and exposure to structures before crews are committed to a line assignment.
The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine compares recent reconnaissance observations with camera detections and weather-driven projections to support tactical recommendations.
The Smoke Classifier Module remains a supporting source during suppression planning and is not treated as the sole basis for aircraft commitment.
The Air Attack Supervisor uses the Wind Shift Bulletin to reassess aircraft sequencing, holding areas, and drop approach direction.
The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console maintains a planning view of tanker availability, estimated time to target, base turnaround time, and assigned incident priority.
Marigold must prevent a dispatch plan from being released when required aviation approvals, airspace status, or tanker readiness fields are incomplete.
The Airspace Restricted State limits dispatch options until the Air Attack Supervisor confirms that the planned route and working altitude are acceptable.
The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console produces the Runway Release Note after the planned departure sequence has been validated against runway constraints.
The Tanker Base Manager uses the batch slip to confirm that the loading record matches the aircraft assignment and planned retardant quantity.
The East Retardant Loading Pump and West Retardant Loading Pump report equipment state, flow readiness, and out-of-service conditions to support base capacity estimates.
Loading status is displayed as operational information rather than as an approval, so a supervisor decision is still required before aircraft are committed.
The Tanker Base Manager resolves discrepancies in loading status before the dispatch plan is presented as ready for release.
The VHF Radio Gateway Repeater provides an operational fallback for relaying approved aviation instructions when data connectivity is degraded.
The Crewline Mobile Tablet shows approved suppression objectives, aircraft caution areas, and current assignment notes for crews operating near the incident.
The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges nearby aircraft activity before personnel are moved into a drop zone or a reconnaissance overflight area.
The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console sends the Suppression Drop Receipt after a completed drop has been recorded and checked for required timing fields.
During extended attack, the Caldera Incident Command Portal preserves each aviation decision with the approving supervisor, operational period, and reason for change.
The County Emergency Liaison can view approved aviation status and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter dispatch or suppression records.
If reconnaissance, loading status, or weather guidance conflicts with an active plan, the system holds the affected recommendation for Air Attack Supervisor review before further action.
